criteria_coverage.criterion: An approved taxonomy of subjects and an approved taxonomy of year levels exist as reference data, each entry having a stable identifier and a human-readable display label.
covered_by: exports exactly six entries
every subject has a non-empty string id and label
contains exactly the approved MVP subject labels (any order)
subject IDs are unique
subject IDs are stable non-numeric slugs
exports exactly three entries
every year level has a non-empty string id and label
contains exactly the approved MVP year-level labels (any order)
year-level IDs are unique
year-level IDs are stable non-numeric slugs
subject IDs and year-level IDs are disjoint (no shared ID)
criteria_coverage.notes: All contract invariants for Interface 1 are thoroughly tested: lengths, label membership, unique IDs, non-numeric slugs, and ID namespace disjointness.

criteria_coverage.criterion: The taxonomy reference data is retrievable by the application (e.g. so creation and filter UIs can present the approved options).
covered_by: returns an object with subjects equal to SUBJECTS and yearLevels equal to YEAR_LEVELS
returned object has exactly the keys subjects and yearLevels
returns 200 with application/json content-type and correct top-level shape
response contains all six subjects with correct shape and approved labels
response contains all three year levels with correct shape and approved labels
criteria_coverage.notes: Both the service function and the HTTP endpoint are tested for correct shape, content, and status.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Creating a resource requires a subject selection and a year-level selection; a submission missing either is rejected.
covered_by: rejects an empty array with TaxonomyValidationError reason 'empty' (validateSubjectIds)
rejects an empty array with TaxonomyValidationError reason 'empty' (validateYearLevelIds)
criteria_coverage.notes: Empty-array rejection for both validators encodes the 'at least one required' invariant. The actual resource creation flow is owned by #4, not this ticket.

criteria_coverage.criterion: The API rejects any resource create/update whose subject or year-level value is not part of the approved taxonomy, returning a clear validation error rather than silently accepting or dropping it.
covered_by: rejects an array with one unknown subject ID with TaxonomyValidationError reason 'unknown-ids'
rejects a mix of one valid and one unknown subject ID (no partial acceptance)
rejects a year-level ID passed as a subject ID
rejects an array with one unknown year-level ID with TaxonomyValidationError reason 'unknown-ids'
rejects a mix of one valid and one unknown year-level ID (no partial acceptance)
rejects a subject ID passed as a year-level ID
criteria_coverage.notes: The rejection paths are well-tested for correct error class and reason. However, the unknownIds property is NOT asserted in the 'unknown-ids' cases — the contract requires unknownIds to be populated with the offending strings. A buggy implementation that throws with reason 'unknown-ids' but an empty unknownIds array would pass all these tests. See finding F1.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Editing an existing resource re-validates subject and year level against the same taxonomy, so tags stay within the approved set after edits.
criteria_coverage.notes: The validation functions themselves are well-tested and would be called during edits. However, the edit flow is owned by #4/#5. No test explicitly exercises an 'edit revalidation' scenario, but the contract doesn't define an edit-specific interface either — the same validateSubjectIds/validateYearLevelIds are reused. Acceptable given scope.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Resource cards and resource detail views display the resource's subject and year-level tags in a clearly readable way.
criteria_coverage.notes: Out of scope for this ticket — depends on #4 resource UI. The contract explicitly excludes UI display. No finding raised.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Filtering a resource listing by a subject and/or a year level returns only resources tagged with the selected value(s), and clearing the filter restores the full set.
criteria_coverage.notes: Out of scope for this ticket — depends on #6 search/browse. The contract defines no filtering interface. No finding raised.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Seed/reference data for the MVP taxonomy is available for local development and QA.
covered_by: contains exactly the approved MVP subject labels (any order)
contains exactly the approved MVP year-level labels (any order)
response contains all six subjects with correct shape and approved labels
response contains all three year levels with correct shape and approved labels
criteria_coverage.notes: The in-memory constants ARE the seed data for MVP. Tests verify the exact approved labels are present.

findings.summary: unknownIds property is never asserted in 'unknown-ids' rejection tests
findings.detail: In all six tests that check for reason 'unknown-ids' (three for validateSubjectIds, three for validateYearLevelIds), none asserts the value of error.unknownIds. The contract requires: 'throws TaxonomyValidationError with reason: "unknown-ids" and unknownIds populated with the offending strings.' A buggy implementation could throw with reason 'unknown-ids' but unknownIds: [] (or undefined) and all tests would pass. At minimum, the single-unknown-ID test for each validator should assert that unknownIds contains the offending string (e.g. expect(err.unknownIds).toContain('not-a-real-subject')). The mixed valid+invalid test should assert that only the unknown ID appears in unknownIds (not the valid one).

findings.summary: Return value of validate*Ids on success path is never asserted
findings.detail: The contract states: 'Returns the input cast to SubjectId[]' on success. Tests only assert .not.toThrow() but never check the return value. A buggy implementation that returns undefined, an empty array, or a different array on the success path would not be caught. Add: const result = validateSubjectIds([SUBJECTS[0].id]); expect(result).toEqual([SUBJECTS[0].id]); — and similarly for validateYearLevelIds.

findings.summary: TaxonomyValidationError 'extends Error' invariant is not tested
findings.detail: The contract states: 'Extends Error — instanceof Error is true.' No test checks that a thrown TaxonomyValidationError is also instanceof Error. This matters because incorrect class extension (e.g. a plain object with matching properties) would slip through. Add: expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(Error) in at least one catch block.

findings.summary: error.message non-empty invariant is not tested
findings.detail: Contract states: 'The message property is a non-empty human-readable string suitable for a 422 response body.' No test asserts that error.message is a non-empty string. A thrown TaxonomyValidationError with message '' would pass. Add: expect((err as TaxonomyValidationError).message.length).toBeGreaterThan(0) in at least one catch block.

findings.summary: No-extra-keys check only validates first item in each array
findings.detail: The test 'each subject and year-level item contains exactly the keys id and label (no extra fields)' only checks body.subjects[0] and body.yearLevels[0]. If the implementation added extra fields to items at index 1+ but not index 0, the test would pass. Should iterate all items with forEach, or at minimum spot-check the last item too.
